commonNameFr: Chien de prairie à queue noire
fieldMarks: Largest Cynomys; 700-1,500 g, 28-33 cm nose to rump, tail 7-10 cm
Dark cinnamon back and upper sides, buff underside
Distal third of tail black or dark brown
behavior: Active by day; rests in burrows in the hottest part of the day
Colonial, with 12 distinct calls including the 'jump-yip'
Mainly grasses and herbs; may reduce activity in winter (no torpor observed in a Colorado study)
habitat: Dry, flat or gently sloping open grassland with short sparse vegetation, including overgrazed pasture; most abundant in mixed-grass and short-grass associations.
range: In Canada, limited to the Frenchman River Valley in southeastern Saskatchewan. In the US from eastern and central Montana and western North Dakota south to Texas and eastern New Mexico; extirpated from Arizona by the 1960s and since reintroduced.
